rw: Web scraping uses programs to automatically extract data from websites, such as prices or headlines, and save it in a structured form for later analysis.

ww.Building a site with code, text and imag: Building a website from code, text and images is web development, not scraping, which instead pulls existing data out of pages that someone else already built.
ww.Cleaning a screen with a cloth and a spr: Cleaning a screen with a cloth and spray is device maintenance and has nothing to do with software, so it cannot describe a data collection technique.
ww.Encrypting pages so that only users can: Encrypting pages so only users can read them is a security practice for protecting content, while scraping is about collecting publicly visible data, not hiding it.

rw: A CSV file is a plain-text file where values are separated by commas, so each line holds one row and any spreadsheet or program can read it easily.

ww.A program that runs on a computer to do: A program that runs on a computer to do a set task is an application or executable, whereas a CSV file only stores data and cannot run anything.
ww.A picture file such as a photo, saved in: A photo saved in a standard format is an image file such as JPEG or PNG, which stores pixels, not comma separated rows of text values.
ww.A video file such as a clip, saved in a: A clip saved in a standard format is a video file such as MP4, which stores moving frames and sound, not plain text values split by commas.

rw: JSON is a lightweight text format for structured data using key-value pairs, which makes it easy for people to read and for programs and web services to exchange.

ww.A database that stores tables of records: A database that stores tables and lets users search them is something like SQL storage, while JSON is only a text format used to write data, not a search engine.
ww.A type of image file, such as a photo sa: An image file type holds pixels, but JSON is plain text describing data with keys and values, so it cannot be a photo format at all.
ww.A programming language only, used to bui: JSON is not a programming language, since it has no loops or logic, and it is used far beyond websites to hold and move structured data of every kind.

rw: A Python library is a collection of pre-written code that others can reuse, so programmers import tools like pandas instead of writing common functions from scratch every time.

ww.A database that stores records in tables: A database that stores records in tables is a data storage system, but a Python library is a bundle of ready made code that programmers import into their own scripts.
ww.A book building where readers borrow and: A building where readers borrow books is a real library, and the word is only a loose analogy here, since a Python library is code and not a place.
ww.A hardware part that fits inside a compu: A hardware part inside a computer case is a physical component such as a drive, but a Python library is software made of code that can be reused.

rw: An IDE is an integrated development environment, a single program that combines a code editor, debugger and testing tools so developers can write and test code efficiently.

ww.A database that stores tables of records: A database that stores tables of records is a data store, while an IDE is the application where programmers write, run and debug their code in one place.
ww.A chart that shows values as bars, lines: A chart showing values as bars, lines or slices is a data visualization, and it is not a tool for editing source code or testing programs.
ww.An internet device such as a router or a: A router, modem or cable box is networking hardware that connects devices to the internet, whereas an IDE is software used by developers to write and test code.

rw: AutoML is a set of tools that automate steps of building machine learning models, such as choosing features, picking algorithms and tuning settings, which saves time and expert effort.

ww.A database that stores records in tables: A database that stores records in tables is a data store that holds information, but AutoML is about automating model building rather than storing business records.
ww.A car manual that lists parts, fuel type: A car manual lists parts and repair steps for vehicles, which has no link to machine learning, since AutoML is software that helps build predictive models automatically.
ww.A manual spreadsheet where cells are fil: A spreadsheet filled by hand is a manual process, which is the opposite of AutoML, because AutoML exists precisely to automate the work of building models.

rw: Bias in the training data is the cause: past hiring records mostly from men teach the model to favor male patterns, so it ranks women lower.

ww.The model has no data: The model having no data cannot be the cause, because it was trained on past hiring data that mostly came from men, so data existed but was skewed.
ww.The model is too accurate: Being too accurate does not explain unfair rankings, because the problem is that the model accurately copies a skewed history, so the fault lies in the data, not accuracy.
ww.The computer is too slow: A slow computer only affects how long training or scoring takes, and it cannot make a model systematically rank women lower than men in its results.

rw: Explainable AI refers to methods that make AI decisions understandable to humans, so people can see why a model gave a result and can trust or challenge it.

ww.AI that hides its logic from users so de: AI that hides its logic is the black box problem, which is the opposite of explainable AI, whose whole goal is to make decisions open and understandable.
ww.AI without data, a system that has nothi: AI without data has nothing to learn from and could not make decisions at all, whereas explainable AI is about clarifying how a working model reaches its outputs.
ww.AI that explains jokes and riddles to pe: AI that explains jokes is just a language task for entertainment, while XAI is a field focused on making a model's own decision process transparent and reviewable.

rw: The black box problem is that it is hard to understand how some complex models, like deep neural networks, reach their decisions, which makes them difficult to audit or trust.

ww.A security feature that locks files with: A security feature that locks files with a code is encryption or password protection, which is unrelated to the black box problem, a matter of model transparency.
ww.Flight recorders that store data from an: Flight recorders store aircraft data after a crash and are literally called black boxes, but that is aviation equipment and not the AI transparency issue asked about.
ww.A hardware box that holds a computer's p: A hardware box holding a computer's parts is a case or chassis, which is about physical housing and has no connection to understanding AI decision making.

rw: GDPR is a European Union law that protects personal data and privacy, giving people rights over how organizations collect, store and use information about them.

ww.A banking rule that sets the interest ra: A banking rule setting loan interest rates would be financial regulation, but GDPR deals with personal data protection and not with interest rates on loans.
ww.A U.S. tax law that sets the rates of in: A U.S. tax law setting income tax rates is not GDPR, which is a European data protection regulation and has nothing to do with taxation in the United States.
ww.A trade treaty that sets duties on goods: A trade treaty setting duties on goods is about tariffs and commerce, whereas GDPR is a privacy law governing how personal data is handled.

rw: CCPA is a California law that gives residents rights over their personal data, including the rights to know what is collected, to delete it and to opt out of its sale.

ww.A trade law that sets tariffs on goods t: A trade law setting tariffs on imports concerns customs duties, while CCPA is a California privacy law about personal data, so tariffs are not its subject.
ww.A bank rule that limits how much a custo: A bank rule limiting daily withdrawals is a financial policy, which has nothing to do with CCPA, a law that protects how businesses handle consumer personal data.
ww.A federal tax that businesses pay on all: A federal tax on business profits is a revenue measure, but CCPA is a state law from California and it covers privacy rights, not taxes of any kind.

rw: Data minimization means collecting only the data needed for a specific purpose, which lowers privacy risk and exposure if a breach happens and respects the people involved.

ww.Keeping data forever, long after it has: Keeping data forever, long after it has any use, is the opposite of minimization, because holding unneeded data raises privacy risk and breach exposure without any benefit.
ww.Collecting as much as possible in case i: Collecting as much as possible in case it is useful later is the opposite of minimization, since it gathers data with no stated purpose and adds needless risk.
ww.Selling extra data to other firms that p: Selling extra data to other firms is a monetization practice that spreads personal data further, so it goes against minimization, which aims to limit how much is held.

rw: The main concern is misinformation and harm to reputation, because a convincing fake video can make viewers believe a public figure said something false and damage their name.

ww.Lower storage costs for the whole firm: Lower storage costs are not a concern with a fake video, since the real harm of a deepfake is deceiving viewers, not the price of keeping files.
ww.Faster internet speeds for most users: Faster internet speeds have no link to a fabricated video, which is a content authenticity problem that can mislead people no matter how quickly it spreads online.
ww.Better camera quality and sharper video: Better camera quality is irrelevant, since a deepfake is generated by AI rather than filmed, and the worry is that fake footage looks real enough to deceive.

rw: Human oversight matters because humans can catch errors, bias and unintended consequences that a model misses, which is vital when decisions affect health, money, safety or rights.

ww.AI never errs and so humans need not che: Claiming AI never errs is false, since models make mistakes and show bias, which is exactly why humans must check high-stakes decisions rather than skip review.
ww.It slows all work for no reason, since p: Saying oversight slows work for no reason ignores the benefit, because for high-stakes decisions the short delay is worth it to catch harmful mistakes before they cause damage.
ww.It removes accountability from people an: Removing accountability from people is the opposite of the goal, since oversight keeps a named person responsible for the outcome instead of blaming a machine.

rw: Fairness in AI means systems should treat individuals and groups equitably without unjust bias, so similar people get similar outcomes and no group is harmed without reason.

ww.Ignoring affected people when a system m: Ignoring affected people is a failure of fairness, since fair systems consider how decisions impact the people they touch and give them a voice and a way to appeal.
ww.Always favoring majority groups over sma: Always favoring majority groups is itself bias, because fairness requires that smaller groups are not disadvantaged, so putting one group first in every decision breaks the idea.
ww.Treating everyone identically in all cas: Treating everyone identically in all cases can still be unfair when people have different needs or histories, so fairness aims at equitable results, not identical treatment.

rw: The concern is that models may be trained on or reproduce copyrighted works without permission, which raises questions about owners' rights, payment and whether outputs copy protected material.

ww.Models cannot create text, so they canno: Saying models cannot create text is false, because generative models write fluent text and can reproduce passages, which is exactly why copying from others is a concern.
ww.Only hardware is protected by copyright,: Claiming only hardware is protected is wrong, since copyright covers software, writing, images and music, so training data and outputs can raise real legal questions.
ww.Copyright does not apply to anything tha: Saying copyright does not apply to machine made work is too simple, because the concern is about whether protected works were used or copied, and the law is still unsettled.

rw: An ethics review board evaluates AI projects for risks, bias and societal impact, so concerns can be found and fixed before a system is released to the public.

ww.Training models on large data sets for u: Training models on large data sets is the job of engineers and data scientists, while a review board checks whether a project is safe and fair.
ww.Selling AI products to customers in stor: Selling AI products to customers is a sales role, and an ethics board does not market anything, since its purpose is to judge risks and not to earn revenue.
ww.Cleaning data by removing errors and gap: Cleaning data by removing errors is routine data preparation work, whereas an ethics review board looks at the wider harm, fairness and social effect of an AI project.

rw: Surveillance capitalism is an economic model that profits from collecting and analyzing personal data, often to predict and influence behavior and to target advertising at people.

ww.A charity that raises money for good cau: A charity raising money for good causes is a nonprofit, which is the opposite of surveillance capitalism, a profit driven model built around gathering personal data about users.
ww.A camera brand that makes lenses and cam: A camera brand making lenses sells hardware, but surveillance capitalism is an economic model, not a company that makes cameras, and it centers on data about people.
ww.A security business that guards building: A security business guarding buildings with cameras sells protection services, whereas surveillance capitalism describes earning profit by collecting and analyzing people's personal data for prediction and advertising.

rw: The main privacy risk is tracking and identifying people without their knowledge or consent, since faces captured in public can be matched to names and followed over time.

ww.It makes photos blurry and lowers their: Making photos blurry affects image quality only, but the main privacy risk of facial recognition is that it can identify and track real people from their faces.
ww.It improves lighting in rooms by adjusti: Improving the lighting in rooms is an unrelated function of lamps and sensors, and it does not describe how facial recognition puts personal privacy at risk.
ww.It reduces image size so that photos tak: Reducing image size is a compression task that saves disk space, which has no bearing on the privacy risk of being identified by a face matching system.

rw: To audit an AI system means to review its data, performance and outcomes for accuracy and fairness, checking that it works as intended and does not harm any group.

ww.Hide its results so the public cannot se: Hiding results so the public cannot see how decisions are made is the opposite of auditing, which aims to bring transparency and let reviewers check the system's behavior.
ww.Sell the system to another company that: Selling the system to another company is a business deal and not an audit, since an audit examines how the system behaves instead of transferring who owns it.
ww.Delete its code so that nobody can use o: Deleting its code so nobody can use it would destroy the system and any evidence, whereas an audit studies the system and leaves it intact so it can be improved.

rw: Knowledge representation is how information is structured so a computer can use it to reason, for example through rules, graphs or ontologies that encode facts and their links.

ww.Showing slides to an audience in a meeti: Showing slides to an audience is a way of presenting information to people, but knowledge representation is about structuring facts so a computer can store and reason about them.
ww.A hardware part that fits inside a compu: A hardware part that fits inside a computer case is a physical component, while knowledge representation is a software concept about encoding facts and relationships for machines.
ww.A user interface that lets people click: A user interface with buttons and menus is about how people interact with software, which is different from how an AI system structures knowledge for its own reasoning.

rw: An ontology in AI is a formal description of concepts in a domain and the relationships between them, which lets systems share a common vocabulary and reason about it.

ww.A branch of biology that studies plants: Ontology in biology-sounding terms may confuse, but the AI meaning is not a study of plants and animals; it is a structured map of concepts and their links.
ww.A chart type used to show shares of a to: A chart showing shares of a total as slices is a pie chart, a visualization tool, whereas an ontology organizes concepts and relations to represent knowledge.
ww.A database engine that stores tables and: A database engine stores tables and runs queries, but an ontology is a conceptual model of a domain's terms and relationships rather than software for storing rows.

rw: Machine translation is the automatic conversion of text from one language to another by software, as when a tool turns an English sentence into Spanish within seconds.

ww.Typing speed measured in words per minut: Typing speed in words per minute measures how fast a person types, which is a keyboard skill and has no connection to converting text between human languages.
ww.Moving machines from one site to another: Moving machines from one site to another is about logistics and relocation, so it is unrelated to language, and the word translation here refers to text, not transport.
ww.Fixing machines that break down in a fac: Fixing machines that break down in a factory is maintenance work, whereas machine translation is a language technology that converts written or spoken words between languages automatically.

rw: Reasoning in AI means drawing logical conclusions from known facts and rules, for example concluding that a bird can fly unless it is known to be a penguin.

ww.Printing rules on paper so that staff ca: Printing rules on paper only records them for staff to read, but reasoning in AI means a system applies rules to facts to reach new conclusions.
ww.Memorizing data and repeating it back wo: Memorizing data and repeating it back word for word is rote recall, which lacks inference, whereas reasoning draws new conclusions from known facts and rules.
ww.Storing files on a disk or in the cloud: Storing files on a disk or in the cloud is data storage, which keeps information but does not process it to infer anything, so it is not reasoning.

rw: If temperature is above 80, turn on the fan is an if-then rule because it states a condition, temperature above 80, and the action that follows when it is true.

ww.The fan is blue and it sits on the desk: The fan is blue and it sits on the desk is a plain description of a fact, with no condition leading to an action, so it is not an if-then rule.
ww.Fans are useful in hot rooms and offices: Fans are useful in hot rooms and offices is a general statement of opinion or fact, and it has no condition paired with a specific action, so it is no rule.
ww.Temperature is 80 degrees in the room no: Temperature is 80 degrees in the room now only reports a current reading, giving a fact with no condition and no resulting action, so it cannot be an if-then rule.

rw: Sensor fusion means combining data from multiple sensors to get a more accurate picture, as when a self driving car blends camera, radar and lidar readings.

ww.Melting sensors with heat so that they f: Melting sensors with heat to form one part would destroy them, and the term actually refers to merging their data, not physically joining the devices together.
ww.Hiding sensors behind panels so that peo: Hiding sensors behind panels is an installation choice about appearance, and it does not describe sensor fusion, which is about merging readings from several sensors into one view.
ww.Replacing sensors every year with newer: Replacing sensors every year is a maintenance schedule, which does not combine any data, so it fails to describe the way sensor fusion improves accuracy.

rw: Lidar is a sensor that uses laser light to measure distance and build 3D maps, which is why self driving cars use it to see the shape of their surroundings.

ww.A microphone that records sound so a com: A microphone that records sound so a computer can turn it into text is speech input hardware, whereas lidar works with laser light, not sound waves.
ww.A radio that sends out waves to carry a: A radio sending waves to carry a driver's voice between cars is communications gear, but lidar is a sensor measuring distance and not a voice link.
ww.A thermometer that reads heat so a machi: A thermometer reads heat to sense temperature, but lidar measures distance with pulses of laser light and does not measure the warmth of a room.

rw: Edge computing means processing data near where it is generated rather than in a distant data center, which cuts delay, saves bandwidth and helps with devices that need fast responses.

ww.Computing in the cloud only, on remote s: Computing in the cloud only, on remote servers far from the source, is the opposite of edge computing, which moves processing closer to where the data is created.
ww.Computing at the edge of a table, with p: Computing at the edge of a table with a hinge is a silly literal reading, since edge computing is a networking idea and has nothing to do with furniture.
ww.Printing data on paper at the end of a l: Printing data on paper at the end of a shift is a manual reporting task and does not describe processing data close to its source on a device.

rw: The mean is the sum divided by the count: 4 + 8 + 6 + 5 + 7 = 30, and 30 divided by 5 values equals 6.

ww.5: 5 is one of the values in the list, but it is not the mean, since the sum of 30 divided by 5 values gives 6, not 5.
ww.8: 8 is the largest value in the set, which is the maximum, and it is not the mean because the mean is the total divided by the count.
ww.30: 30 is the sum of the values, since 4 + 8 + 6 + 5 + 7 = 30, but the mean needs that sum divided by the 5 values.

rw: Sorting gives 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, and the middle of those five values is 5, so the median is 5.

ww.3: 3 is the smallest value, the minimum, and it sits at the start of the sorted list 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, so it cannot be the median.
ww.9: 9 is the largest value in the set, which makes it the maximum, and it sits at the end of the sorted list, not in the middle position.
ww.5.6: 5.6 is the mean, because 3 + 9 + 4 + 7 + 5 = 28 and 28 divided by 5 is 5.6, whereas the question asks for the median, the middle value.

rw: The mode is the value that appears most often, and 3 appears three times in the list, more than 5 which appears twice or any other value.

ww.5: 5 appears only twice in the list, while 3 appears three times, so 5 is not the most frequent value and cannot be the mode.
ww.7: 7 appears just once in the list 2, 3, 3, 5, 3, 7, 5, so it is a rare value and certainly not the one that occurs most often.
ww.3.7: 3.7 is not even a value in the list, and a mode must be a value that occurs, while the mean here is 28 divided by 7, which equals 4.

rw: The range is the maximum minus the minimum, so 31 - 12 = 19, which measures how far apart the largest and smallest values are.

ww.12: 12 is the smallest value, the minimum, and the range needs the difference between the largest and smallest, which is 31 - 12 = 19.
ww.31: 31 is the largest value, the maximum, but the range subtracts the smallest value from it, giving 31 - 12 = 19 instead.
ww.96: 96 is the sum of all five values, since 12 + 20 + 15 + 31 + 18 = 96, but the range is a difference, not a total.

rw: A fair coin has two equally likely outcomes, heads and tails, so the probability of heads is 1 divided by 2, which equals 0.5.

ww.1: A probability of 1 means certainty, but heads is not guaranteed on a fair coin, which gives heads only half of the time, so 0.5.
ww.2: A probability can never exceed 1, so a value of 2 is impossible, and it also does not match one favorable outcome out of two.
ww.0.25: 0.25 is the chance of getting two heads in a row, since 0.5 x 0.5 = 0.25, but this question flips the coin only once.

rw: There are 3 red marbles out of 10 in total, so the probability of drawing red is 3 divided by 10, which equals 0.3.

ww.3: 3 is the count of red marbles, not a probability, because a probability must be between 0 and 1 and is found by dividing 3 by the total of 10.
ww.0.43: 0.43 comes from comparing 3 red to 7 blue as 3 divided by 7, but the total is 10 marbles, so the chance is 3 divided by 10.
ww.0.7: 0.7 is the probability of drawing a blue marble, since 7 out of 10 are blue, while the question asks about red, which is the other 3 of 10.

rw: Six of the 36 equally likely outcomes sum to 7, namely 1+6, 2+5, 3+4, 4+3, 5+2 and 6+1, so the probability is 6/36, which is 1/6.

ww.1/12: 1/12 would mean 3 favorable outcomes out of 36, but a sum of 7 has 6 ways: 1+6, 2+5, 3+4, 4+3, 5+2, 6+1, giving 6/36.
ww.1/36: 1/36 is the chance of one exact pair such as a 3 and a 4 in order, but a sum of 7 can come from 6 different pairs.
ww.7/36: 7/36 wrongly treats the target sum of 7 as the number of ways to roll it, but the real count of ways is 6, so the answer is 6/36.

rw: For independent events, P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B), so 0.5 x 0.4 = 0.2, meaning both events happen together in about one case in five.

ww.0.9: 0.9 is the sum of 0.5 and 0.4, but for independent events P(A and B) is found by multiplying the two probabilities, not by adding them.
ww.0.1: 0.1 would be the gap between 0.5 and 0.4, but independent events combine by multiplication, and the product is 0.5 x 0.4, which is not 0.1.
ww.0.45: 0.45 is the average of 0.5 and 0.4, but averaging has no role in joint probability, which for independent events is the product 0.5 x 0.4 = 0.2.

rw: A standard deviation of zero means all values in the data set are identical, because each value equals the mean and there is no distance from the center.

ww.The data has a very large spread overall: A very large spread corresponds to a large standard deviation, so it is the opposite of zero, which means no spread at all among the values.
ww.The data set is empty and has no values: An empty data set has no values, so a standard deviation cannot even be computed, and a computed value of zero describes data that exists but does not vary.
ww.The mean is zero so every value is also: A zero standard deviation says nothing about the mean being zero; values such as 5, 5, 5 have a mean of 5 and still have no spread.

rw: A correlation of -0.9 is close to -1, which suggests a strong negative relationship: as one variable rises, the other tends to fall, along a fairly tight line.

ww.No relationship at all between the two v: No relationship at all would give a correlation near 0, but -0.9 is far from zero, which shows a strong link between the two variables.
ww.A strong positive relationship in which: A strong positive relationship would give a coefficient near +1, but the negative sign on -0.9 means the variables move in opposite directions instead of rising together.
ww.That the first variable causes the secon: Correlation alone does not prove one variable causes the other to fall; it only describes how they move together, so a causal claim goes beyond what -0.9 shows.

rw: The sample proportion is the part divided by the whole, so 120 divided by 400 equals 0.30, meaning 30 percent of those surveyed prefer brand A.

ww.0.12: 0.12 would come from dividing 120 by 1,000, but the sample has 400 people, so the proportion is 120 divided by 400, which is 0.30.
ww.3.33: 3.33 is 400 divided by 120, which flips the fraction; a proportion is the part over the whole, 120 divided by 400, and cannot exceed 1.
ww.0.70: 0.70 is the share of people who do not prefer brand A, since 280 of 400 is 0.70, but the question asks about the 120 who do.

rw: A larger sample size usually makes the margin of error smaller, because estimates from more people vary less and sit closer to the true population value.

ww.It has no effect on the margin of error: Saying sample size has no effect is wrong, because the margin of error shrinks roughly with the square root of the sample size as more data adds precision.
ww.It makes the margin of error much larger: A larger sample does not make the margin of error much larger; it moves the other way, since more data reduces sampling variation and tightens the estimate.
ww.It makes the error margin equal to zero: A margin of error never drops to exactly zero for a sample, because only surveying the whole population removes sampling error, so bigger samples only shrink it.

rw: Since the p-value of 0.03 is less than the significance level of 0.05, the result is statistically significant and we reject the null hypothesis.

ww.Fail to reject the null: Failing to reject the null applies when the p-value is above the significance level, but here 0.03 is below 0.05, so the opposite conclusion follows.
ww.Accept the null as proven: Accepting the null as proven is never the right wording, because a test cannot prove the null true, and here p is below 0.05 so it is rejected.
ww.The test is not valid here: Nothing suggests the test is invalid; a p-value of 0.03 is perfectly usable and simply falls below the 0.05 threshold, which leads to a decision to reject.

rw: The median is the middle value of the sorted data, so an extreme outlier at either end does not move it much, which makes it robust.

ww.The mean: The mean uses every value in its calculation, so one extreme outlier can pull it far from the center, which makes it very sensitive to outliers.
ww.The range: The range is the maximum minus the minimum, so an outlier directly changes it, and it is a measure of spread, not a measure of center.
ww.The sum: The sum adds all values, so one extreme outlier changes it a great deal, and a sum is also not a measure of center in the first place.

rw: In a right-skewed set the long tail of high values pulls the mean upward, so the mean is usually greater than the median, which sits closer to the bulk.

ww.The mean is less than the median: A mean below the median is the pattern for a left-skewed set, where a tail of low values drags the mean down, so it is wrong here.
ww.The mode is always the largest value: The mode is the most frequent value and is typically near the peak of the data, which lies on the low side in a right-skewed set, not at the largest value.
ww.The mean always equals the median: The mean and median are equal only in roughly symmetric data, and skew pulls the mean toward the tail, so they are not always equal.

rw: A pie chart is a circle cut into slices sized by proportion, which makes it the best choice for showing how a share of a whole is divided.

ww.A line chart: A line chart shows how a value changes over an ordered sequence such as time, so it does not display how a whole is divided into shares.
ww.A histogram: A histogram shows how often values fall within ranges, or bins, of one numeric variable, which is a distribution and not a split of a whole.
ww.A scatter plot: A scatter plot places points to show the relationship between two numeric variables, so it is not suited to showing how parts share a whole.

rw: A line chart connects points in time order, so rises and falls are easy to follow, which makes it the best chart for showing a trend over time.

ww.A pie chart: A pie chart shows how parts divide a whole at one moment, so it cannot show how a value moves across several time periods.
ww.A name table: A name table lists labels and does not draw any trend, so it fails to make a change over time easy to see at a glance.
ww.A single bar: A single bar shows one value at one moment, so it gives no sequence of points and cannot display a trend over time.

rw: A scatter plot puts one numeric variable on each axis and plots points, so patterns such as upward trends or clusters between the two variables become visible.

ww.A pie chart: A pie chart shows how parts divide a whole, so it cannot display how two numeric variables relate to one another across many observations.
ww.A word cloud: A word cloud sizes words by how often they appear in text, so it shows no numeric relationship between two variables at all.
ww.A bar chart: A bar chart compares values across categories, with one axis holding labels, so it is not designed to show how two numeric variables move together.

rw: A histogram shows how often values fall within ranges, called bins, so you can see the shape of a distribution, such as its center, spread and skew.

ww.Showing a change in a value over a perio: Showing a change in value over a period of days is the job of a line chart, whereas a histogram groups values into ranges and counts them.
ww.Showing the link between two variables a: Showing the link between two variables as points is a scatter plot, while a histogram describes only one variable and counts how many values land in each bin.
ww.Showing how a total is divided into part: Showing how a total is divided into parts is the job of a pie chart, but a histogram instead displays the frequency of values within numeric intervals.

rw: A truncated axis starts above zero, here at 90, which makes bars differ in visible height far more than the true values do and so exaggerates differences.

ww.A confidence interval for each of the va: A confidence interval shows uncertainty around an estimate with error bars, and it has nothing to do with where the vertical axis of a bar chart begins.
ww.A fair chart that shows the true differe: Calling it a fair chart is wrong, since starting at 90 instead of 0 distorts bar lengths and makes a small gap look much larger than it truly is.
ww.A normalization step making all the bars: Normalization rescales data values onto a common range, but moving the axis start changes only the display and leaves the bars unequal, so it is a different thing.

rw: Filling missing values with the mean or median keeps the rows, and removing the affected rows is another common option, so both are accepted ways to handle gaps.

ww.Delete every column so that no missing v: Deleting every column removes all the data, including the useful parts, so it does not handle missing values and would leave nothing to analyze.
ww.Ignore them and treat each one as the nu: Treating every missing value as zero can distort results, because zero is a real number that may differ greatly from the true value, so it is not a safe default.
ww.Replace them with random words to fill t: Replacing missing values with random words would put text into a numeric column and corrupt the data, so it creates errors and does not repair the gaps.

rw: Data cleaning means finding and fixing errors, gaps and duplicates, so that later analysis rests on accurate and complete records that can be trusted for decisions.

ww.Moving the data to a new computer for sa: Moving the data to a new computer is a storage or migration task, and it does not correct any mistakes, gaps or duplicates in the records themselves.
ww.Deleting all of the data to start again: Deleting all the data to start again discards valuable information, whereas cleaning repairs specific problems and keeps the good data in place for analysis.
ww.Making the charts brighter and more colo: Making charts brighter and more colorful is a presentation choice made after analysis, and it does nothing to fix errors or gaps in the underlying data.

rw: A categorical variable places items into groups or labels, such as color, city or type of pet, instead of measuring them on a numeric scale.

ww.A variable whose value is calculated by: A variable calculated by a formula is a computed or derived variable, which says how its value is obtained, while a categorical variable describes the kind of value it holds.
ww.A variable that has the same value in ev: A variable with the same value in every row is a constant, and it carries no information, while a categorical variable usually has several distinct groups.
ww.A variable that takes any numeric value: A variable taking any numeric value in a range is continuous, such as height, which is different from a categorical variable that sorts items into groups.

rw: Asking only students who eat in the cafeteria leaves out those who bring lunch or eat elsewhere, so the sample is not representative, which is sampling bias.

ww.The questions are too long, so results a: Long questions can hurt reliability, but the described flaw is that only cafeteria students were asked, which is who was surveyed, and not how the questions were worded.
ww.The survey is too large to analyze the a: A survey being too large is rarely a problem, and the real issue here is who was left out, not how many responses the survey collected.
ww.The mean is wrongly calculated as it use: The mean may be calculated correctly; the flaw lies earlier, in who was chosen to answer, so even perfect arithmetic would describe only part of the student body.

rw: A pivot table summarizes data by grouping and totaling, for example showing total sales by region or month, without changing the original data in the sheet.

ww.Rotates a screen to show data at an angl: Rotating a screen to show data at an angle is a display setting, while a pivot table is a spreadsheet feature that reorganizes and summarizes data.
ww.Draws pictures of people in the table ro: Drawing pictures of people in the table rows is not a spreadsheet function, and the name pivot refers to turning rows into a grouped summary, not artwork.
ww.Deletes duplicate files to free up disk: Deleting duplicate files frees disk room, but a pivot table works inside a spreadsheet to group and total values, and it does not manage files on a disk.

rw: =SUM(B2:B6) adds the values in cells B2 through B6, giving the total of those five cells in one result.

ww.Counts how many cells in B2 to B6 hold t: Counting cells that hold text uses a function such as COUNTA or COUNTIF, whereas SUM adds numbers together and does not count any cells.
ww.Multiplies the values in B2 through B6: Multiplying values in a range uses the PRODUCT function, but SUM adds them, so =SUM(B2:B6) does not multiply the values in B2 through B6.
ww.Finds the largest value in B2 through B6: Finding the largest value uses the MAX function, while SUM adds the values together, so =SUM(B2:B6) returns a total and not a maximum.

rw: #DIV/0! appears when a formula tries to divide by zero or by an empty cell, which is undefined in math, so the spreadsheet shows this error code.

ww.The cell has too many digits for the col: Too many digits for a column width usually shows as ##### in the cell, which is a display issue and is different from the #DIV/0! error.
ww.The workbook is protected by a user pass: A protected workbook blocks editing or opening and asks for a password, but it does not produce a formula error, and #DIV/0! is about division.
ww.The formula refers to a sheet that has b: A formula that refers to a missing or renamed sheet gives a #REF! error, which differs from #DIV/0!, the code that appears when you divide by zero.

rw: The dollar signs in $A$1 lock both the column and the row, so when the formula is copied it stays fixed on that cell.

ww.It moves to the next cell down: Moving to the next cell down is what a relative reference does when copied down a column, while an absolute reference does not move at all.
ww.It formats the cell as currency: Formatting a cell as currency is done with a number format, and the dollar signs in $A$1 lock the reference rather than change how the value looks.
ww.It deletes that cell entirely: An absolute reference only points to a cell, so copying a formula never deletes the cell it refers to, and the $ signs simply keep the address fixed.

rw: Scaling puts features on similar ranges so that features with large numbers, like incomes in dollars, do not dominate ones with small numbers, like heights in centimeters.

ww.To make all values the same, so no varia: Scaling does not make all values the same, since that would erase the variation that analysis needs, and it only puts features on comparable ranges.
ww.To change the data's meaning so results: Scaling does not change the meaning of the data, since it only rescales numbers, and it should never be done to make results look better.
ww.To remove the need for data cleaning bef: Scaling does not replace cleaning, because errors, gaps and duplicates still need to be fixed, and scaling only adjusts the size of the numbers.

rw: SELECT * FROM customers returns all columns for all rows in the customers table, because the asterisk stands for every column and no WHERE clause filters the rows.

ww.Deletes every row in the customers table: Deleting every row while keeping the table is done with a DELETE statement, whereas SELECT only reads data and never removes anything from the table.
ww.Returns only the first column of the cus: Returning only the first column would need SELECT with that column's name, but the asterisk means all columns, so more than one column comes back.
ww.Creates a new table called customers wit: Creating a new table is done with CREATE TABLE, but SELECT reads from a table that already exists, and it never builds one with no columns.

rw: COUNT(*) returns the number of rows in a table or result, since it counts every row whether or not individual columns hold values.

ww.The max column value: The maximum value of a column is returned by MAX, not COUNT, and COUNT(*) reports how many rows there are and not how big a value is.
ww.The mean column value: The mean of a column is returned by the AVG function, but COUNT(*) only counts rows and does no averaging of any column values.
ww.The column value sum: The sum of column values is returned by the SUM function, whereas COUNT(*) simply tallies rows and does not add up the numbers inside them.

rw: Data quality is how accurate, complete, consistent and timely data is, because data with these traits can be trusted when making decisions and building models.

ww.How colorful and attractive a chart of t: How attractive a chart looks is about presentation and design, but data quality refers to qualities of the data itself, such as accuracy and completeness.
ww.How many people can access a data set at: How many people can access a data set describes availability or permissions, which is not a measure of whether the data itself is correct or complete.
ww.How large a file is when the data is sav: File size on a disk tells how much space the data takes up, but a large file can still be full of errors, so size says nothing about quality.

rw: ETL stands for Extract, transform, load: data is pulled from sources, cleaned and reshaped, then loaded into a target such as a data warehouse.

ww.Estimate, track, log costs: Estimate, track, log costs is not a data process, and ETL describes moving data through three set steps: extract, transform and load.
ww.Enter, trace, label files: Enter, trace, label files does not match any data pipeline, and the letters ETL stand for extract, transform and load, not those actions.
ww.Edit, test, launch a site: Edit, test, launch a site describes web publishing, which is not what ETL means, since ETL is a pipeline that moves and reshapes data.

rw: CSV is a plain-text file format where values are separated by commas, so each line is a row and any spreadsheet or program can open it easily.

ww.A secure format that encrypts data so on: A secure format that encrypts data is something else; CSV stores plain readable text with no encryption, so anyone who opens the file can read it.
ww.A programming language used to write pho: A programming language for phone apps has logic and syntax, but CSV is only a data format that holds values and cannot run code of any kind.
ww.A type of chart that shows how a total i: A chart showing a total divided into parts is a pie chart, which is a visual display, whereas CSV is a file format for storing rows of data.

rw: An API lets programs request data or services from one another, for example a weather app asking a server for a forecast using a defined set of rules.

ww.Counting inventory by hand each night wi: Counting inventory by hand is a manual task that needs no software interface, whereas an API lets one program talk to another and exchange data automatically.
ww.Cleaning errors from a data set with no: Cleaning errors from a data set is data preparation work, which is not what an API does, since an API is an interface for requests between programs.
ww.Printing reports from a database with pa: Printing reports from a database is a reporting task, and an API is not a printing tool but a way for software systems to communicate.

rw: Version control tracks changes to files and lets earlier versions be restored, so a team can see who changed what and roll back mistakes.

ww.Blocking all users from changing a file: Blocking all users from changing a file would defeat teamwork, whereas version control lets many people edit while the history of changes is recorded and can be reviewed.
ww.Deleting all earlier versions so that on: Deleting earlier versions so only the newest file remains is the opposite of version control, which keeps the full history so past states can be recovered.
ww.Making files larger so that they take up: Making files larger and using more disk space is not a goal, since version control stores changes efficiently and its purpose is history and recovery, not size.

rw: Git tracks changes to code and files over time, so developers can see the history, work in parallel on branches and go back to earlier versions when needed.

ww.Stores large data sets in a cloud accoun: Storing large data sets in a cloud account is cloud storage work, while Git is a tool for tracking changes in code and files over time.
ww.Checks grammar and fixes spelling mistak: Checking grammar and fixing spelling is done by a proofreading tool, and Git has no language features because it records changes to files, not writing quality.
ww.Translates code from one language to ano: Translating code from one language to another is done by a transpiler or converter, and Git does not rewrite code, since it just records its history.

rw: A no-code AI tool lets users build simple AI solutions without writing programs, usually through drag and drop screens, so non programmers can create useful models.

ww.A tool that only trained engineers with: A tool only trained engineers can use is the opposite of no-code, which is designed so that people without programming skills can build things themselves.
ww.A tool that requires users to write ever: Requiring users to write every line of code by hand is the opposite of no-code, since these tools replace typing programs with visual building blocks.
ww.A tool that removes all errors from a pr: No tool removes all errors from a program without human review, and no-code does not mean error free; it only means users do not write the code.

rw: RPA uses software bots that perform repetitive, rule-based tasks, such as copying data between systems or filling forms, following fixed steps just as a person would.

ww.Programs that learn from data to predict: Programs that learn from data to predict prices describe machine learning, whereas RPA bots follow fixed rules and do not learn or predict anything.
ww.Physical robots that move paper around f: Despite the word robotic, RPA is not physical robots moving paper; the bots are software programs working on a computer screen and systems.
ww.Machines that build cars on an assembly: Machines that build cars with welding are industrial robots in manufacturing, while RPA refers to software that automates office tasks, not to hardware on a line.

rw: A firewall is a security tool that controls traffic into and out of a network by following rules, blocking connections that are unauthorized or look unsafe.

ww.A program that speeds up a network by co: A program that compresses files to speed up a network is a compression or optimization tool, while a firewall filters traffic to protect the network.
ww.A tool that stores backups of files on a: Storing backups on a remote server is a backup service, which protects against data loss but does not filter traffic as a firewall does.
ww.A wall that stops fires in buildings, ma: A wall that stops fires in buildings is a physical safety barrier, and in computing the name is only an analogy for a network security barrier.

rw: A software update fixes issues and improves security or features, which is why installing updates promptly protects against known vulnerabilities and brings improvements.

ww.Deleting all data stored in the software: Deleting all data stored in the software would destroy information, whereas a software update fixes issues and adds improvements while leaving the user's data in place.
ww.Making the software slower to save batte: Updates are not meant to make software slower to save battery power, since their purpose is to fix bugs, close security holes and add useful features.
ww.Removing user accounts no longer in use: Removing unused user accounts is an administrative cleanup, which is not the aim of a software update, a release that improves the program itself.

rw: Finding the shortest route is search: the app explores many possible paths through the road network and picks the best one, for example with an algorithm like A star.

ww.Generating new roads on the map to short: Generating new roads on the map would be creating content, but the app only uses the roads that exist and picks the shortest route between them.
ww.Recognizing faces in photos along the ro: Recognizing faces in photos is a computer vision task, which has no role in picking the quickest road between two cities on a map.
ww.Writing a poem about each town the drive: Writing a poem about each town is a text generation task, and it has nothing to do with computing the shortest path between two cities.

rw: Collaborative filtering recommends items because users with similar histories liked them, which matches the example of a show suggested from the watch histories of similar people.

ww.Rule-based programming: Rule-based programming follows fixed rules written by people, but this service recommends shows from the viewing habits of similar users, which is learned from data.
ww.Speech recognition tools: Speech recognition tools turn spoken words into text, which has no connection to suggesting shows based on what similar viewers liked.
ww.Optical character reading: Optical character reading converts images of printed text into digital text, so it plays no part in recommending shows from viewing habits.

rw: Sorting emails into spam or not spam means assigning each email to a category, which is classification, a supervised learning task with discrete labels.

ww.Compression: Compression reduces the size of data for storage, and it does not assign emails to labelled groups, so it cannot describe a spam filter.
ww.Clustering: Clustering groups similar items without predefined labels, but here the labels spam and not spam are known in advance, so the task is classification.
ww.Regression: Regression predicts a continuous number, such as a price, whereas a spam filter picks between two categories, so regression does not fit.

rw: Predicting a price from size and location means estimating a continuous number, which is regression, whereas classification would choose among labelled categories.

ww.Reinforcement: Reinforcement learning trains an agent through rewards and penalties from its actions, but predicting a house price from known examples is a supervised task.
ww.Clustering: Clustering groups similar items without labels, but here the model predicts a specific price value learned from past sales, so clustering does not fit.
ww.Classification: Classification assigns items to categories, but a price is a continuous number rather than a category, so this is not a classification task.

rw: Grouping customers by similar buying habits without predefined categories is clustering, an unsupervised technique that finds natural groups by itself in the data.

ww.Image reading: Image reading handles pictures, but the store is grouping customers by buying habits, which involves numbers describing purchases and not images.
ww.Classification: Classification needs predefined labels to learn from, but here there are no set categories, so the groups must be discovered, which is clustering.
ww.Regression: Regression predicts a numeric value, but the goal here is to form groups of similar customers, not to estimate a number such as spending.

rw: Always predicting negative is correct for 99 out of 100 cases, so accuracy is 99 percent, which is misleading because it finds none of the positives.

ww.50 percent, as it guesses one class: 50 percent would be the accuracy of a coin flip on balanced data, but this model gets all 99 negatives right out of 100, so its accuracy is far higher.
ww.100 percent, as it never errs: A model that always predicts negative misses every positive case, so it is wrong on 1 percent of examples and cannot reach 100 percent accuracy.
ww.1 percent, since it predicts none: 1 percent is the share of positive cases, but the model predicts negative every time and is right on the 99 percent that are negative.

rw: Linear regression predicts a continuous numerical value, such as a price or temperature, by fitting a straight line through the data points.

ww.A group of similar items: Finding a group of similar items is clustering, an unsupervised task, while linear regression predicts a number from input values.
ww.The next move of a player: Predicting the next move of a player is more like game playing or sequence modeling, and linear regression predicts numbers from features.
ww.A category such as spam or not: Choosing a category such as spam or not spam is classification, which uses methods like logistic regression, and not a numerical prediction from a line.

rw: Informed consent means people understand how their data will be used and agree to it, so their agreement is a real choice made with full knowledge.

ww.Data is collected from a third party who: Collecting data from a third party that gave permission lacks the consent of the people themselves, who may never have been told or asked.
ww.Data is collected without telling anyone: Collecting data without telling anyone and using it for any purpose is the opposite of informed consent, because people had no knowledge and no choice.
ww.Data is collected after a click without: A click without reading anything is not informed, because people did not learn how their data would be used, so their agreement is not meaningful consent.

rw: The main risk is misinformation and harm to reputation, because a realistic fake of a public figure can spread false claims that many viewers will believe.

ww.A faster internet connection for viewers: A faster internet connection is a benefit for viewers and not a risk, whereas the danger of a fake video is that people believe false claims.
ww.Better camera quality and sharper video: Better camera quality is not a risk of AI made video, since the footage is generated rather than filmed, and the issue is deceiving viewers.
ww.Lower cost of making news programs: Lower cost of making news programs is an efficiency gain and not a harm, while the main risk of a deepfake is false information that damages people.

rw: The copyright concern is whether protected works were used without permission, since training on books, images or articles without a license may infringe the owners' rights.

ww.Whether the model runs faster on one bra: Whether a model runs faster on one brand of hardware is a performance question, and it has no bearing on legal rights over the training material.
ww.Whether the data is stored in the cloud: Whether data is stored in the cloud or on a disk is a storage choice, and it does not decide whether using the works was legally allowed.
ww.Whether the training computer is the cor: Whether the training computer is the correct size is a technical detail about equipment, and it has no relation to the legal rights of the work's creators.

rw: Auditing regularly helps find errors, bias or harmful outcomes that appear over time, since data and conditions change and a system that once worked well can drift.

ww.To make the system more costly, since au: Audits do add some cost, but making the system costlier is a side effect and not the reason to audit, which is to protect people and results.
ww.To prove that the system is perfect and: An audit cannot prove a system is perfect, and no AI system is, so regular audits exist to find issues that need changes and not to claim flawlessness.
ww.To replace the system with a new one eve: Replacing the system every month is wasteful and is not the purpose of an audit, which reviews how the current system performs and decides whether it needs fixes.

rw: A long, unique password for each account, kept in a password manager, resists guessing and limits damage if one site is breached, which makes it a strong practice.

ww.Writing passwords on a note stuck to the: Writing passwords on a note stuck to the monitor lets anyone passing by read and use them, so it is an insecure habit and not a strong practice.
ww.Using one simple password everywhere, ch: Using one simple password everywhere means a single leak exposes every account, and changing it only when a site asks leaves it weak and reused.
ww.Using the name of a pet and a birth year: A pet name and birth year are easy to remember but also easy for attackers to guess from social media, which makes the password weak and predictable.

rw: Ransomware is malware that locks data or systems until a ransom is paid, usually by encrypting files and demanding payment in return for a key.

ww.A tool that finds and removes viruses on: A tool that finds and removes viruses is antivirus software, which defends against threats, whereas ransomware is the harmful program that holds data hostage.
ww.A program that speeds up a computer by d: A program that speeds up a computer by deleting junk is a cleanup utility, while ransomware is malicious software that demands money from its victim.
ww.A bank loan program for small firms shor: A bank loan program for firms short of cash is a finance product, and the word ransom in ransomware refers to a demand made by criminals.

rw: Malware is software designed to harm or steal from a computer, for example viruses, spyware and ransomware that damage systems or take data without consent.

ww.Software that speeds up a computer by de: Software that speeds up a computer by deleting its files describes a cleaning utility at best, whereas malware is built to cause harm and not to help.
ww.Software that checks spelling and gramma: Software that checks spelling and grammar is a useful writing tool, which is harmless and so the opposite of malware, a harmful program.
ww.Software that backs up files and stores: Software that backs up files and stores them online protects data, and it is a legitimate tool, whereas malware works against the user.

rw: The right first steps are to contain the breach to stop further loss and notify affected people as required, so they can protect themselves quickly.

ww.Hide the problem from customers to prote: Hiding the problem from customers delays their chance to protect themselves, and many laws require prompt notice, so concealment makes the damage and the penalties worse.
ww.Blame the customers for weak passwords a: Blaming customers for weak passwords shifts responsibility and does nothing to stop the breach, so it fails the duty to act and to help those affected.
ww.Delete the evidence of the breach so nob: Deleting the evidence destroys the information needed to learn what happened and may break the law, so it blocks the investigation and makes recovery harder.

rw: Access control limits who can view or change data based on their role, so staff see only what their job needs and sensitive records stay protected.

ww.Letting everyone see all records so staf: Letting everyone see all records lowers protection, because people who do not need the data can read or misuse it, which is the reverse of access control.
ww.Storing data on a remote server so nobod: Storing data on a remote server so nobody can reach it makes the data useless, while access control still lets the right people use data safely.
ww.Counting how many times the data is read: Counting how many times data is read is logging or monitoring, which can help with audits but does not itself decide who is allowed in.

rw: A data privacy notice is a statement telling customers what data is collected and how it is used, so they can make informed choices about sharing information.

ww.A message that tells customers their dat: A message saying data will be sold to the highest bidder is not what a notice is for, since it must explain collection and use honestly to customers.
ww.A list of customers' credit card numbers: A list of credit card numbers kept in a file would itself be a serious privacy failure, and a notice never publishes customers' private details.
ww.A bill sent to customers for the cost of: A bill for the cost of storing data is a financial document, whereas a privacy notice explains data practices to customers and does not charge any fee.

rw: Regulation matters because rules can set limits on risky uses and require safeguards, so businesses must plan for compliance and avoid fines, harm and lost trust.

ww.Rules never apply to AI systems, so firm: Saying rules never apply to AI is false, since laws on privacy, bias and safety already cover many AI uses, and firms that ignore them risk penalties.
ww.Rules exist only for large firms, and sm: Rules are not limited to large firms, because many laws apply to organizations of every size, so small businesses cannot safely ignore them when using AI.
ww.Rules guarantee that every AI system mak: Rules cannot guarantee perfect decisions, as no system is flawless, and regulation aims to reduce harm and set duties instead of promising perfection.

rw: Precision is true positives divided by all predicted positives: 40 / (40 + 10) = 40 / 50 = 0.8, so the precision is 80 percent.

ww.20 percent: 20 percent is the share of predicted positives that were wrong, 10 / 50, which is the false discovery rate, and it is not the precision of 40 / 50.
ww.67 percent: 67 percent comes from 40 / (40 + 20), which is the recall because it uses false negatives, whereas precision uses false positives in the denominator.
ww.50 percent: 50 percent does not match the counts; precision is 40 / (40 + 10) = 0.8, so a value of 50 percent would need as many false positives as true ones.

rw: Recall is true positives divided by actual positives: 40 / (40 + 20) = 40 / 60, which is about 0.67, so roughly 67 percent of real positives were found.

ww.About 80 percent: About 80 percent is the precision, 40 / (40 + 10), because it uses false positives, whereas recall divides by true positives plus false negatives.
ww.About 50 percent: About 50 percent does not follow from the counts, since recall is 40 / (40 + 20), which is well above one half and so cannot equal 50 percent.
ww.About 25 percent: About 25 percent is far too low, because recall is 40 divided by 60 actual positives, which is about two thirds, and not a quarter of them.

rw: The F1 score is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, so it is high only when both are high, giving one balanced figure for a classifier.

ww.The time taken to train a model on data: The time taken to train a model is a measure of training duration, while the F1 score measures prediction quality, combining precision and recall into one value.
ww.The share of correct predictions overall: The share of correct predictions overall is accuracy, a separate metric, and the F1 score focuses on positive predictions by balancing precision and recall.
ww.The simple sum of precision and recall: The simple sum of precision and recall would range up to 2 and ignores balance, whereas F1 uses a harmonic mean, which stays between 0 and 1.

rw: F1 = 2 x (precision x recall) / (precision + recall) = 2 x 0.25 / 1.0 = 0.5, so when both values are 0.5 the F1 score is also 0.5.

ww.0.25: 0.25 is the product of precision and recall, 0.5 x 0.5, but F1 is 2 x (0.5 x 0.5) / (0.5 + 0.5), which equals 0.5.
ww.0.0: An F1 of 0.0 occurs only when precision or recall is zero, but here both equal 0.5, so the harmonic mean is 0.5 and not zero.
ww.1.0: An F1 of 1.0 needs perfect precision and recall, and with both at 0.5 the harmonic mean cannot exceed that value, so it equals 0.5.

rw: AUC summarizes how well a classifier separates the classes across all thresholds, with 1.0 meaning perfect separation and 0.5 meaning no better than chance.

ww.How much memory a model needs while it r: Memory needed while running is a resource measure, and AUC says nothing about it, since it is computed from predicted scores and true labels.
ww.How many features a model uses to make e: The number of features a model uses is a design detail, whereas AUC summarizes how well the classifier ranks positives above negatives across thresholds.
ww.How long a model takes to train, as time: Training time is measured with a clock, and AUC is a performance metric computed from predictions, so it says nothing about how long training took.

rw: An AUC of 0.5 means the classifier ranks positives above negatives only half the time, which equals random guessing and shows no useful separation of the classes.

ww.Perfect at separating the classes: Perfect separation of the classes corresponds to an AUC of 1.0, so a value of 0.5 is far from perfect and sits at the chance level.
ww.Faster than most other models: AUC measures how well classes are separated and not speed, so a value of 0.5 says nothing about the model being faster than other models.
ww.Always wrong about the classes: Always being wrong would give an AUC near 0, which is informative since flipping its output would fix it, while 0.5 means no signal at all.

rw: K-fold cross-validation splits the data into k parts, then trains and tests k times, each time holding out a different part, to give a more reliable estimate.

ww.Removing k features from the data before: Removing k features before training is feature selection, whereas k-fold cross-validation keeps all the features and instead rotates which part of the data is held out for testing.
ww.Training a model k times on the same dat: Training k times on the same unchanged split would give the same result each time, but k-fold cross-validation changes the held-out part on every one of its runs.
ww.Testing a model on the training data onl: Testing only on the training data hides overfitting, because the model has already seen those examples, whereas cross-validation always tests on data held out of training.

rw: The bias-variance tradeoff balances a model that is too simple, with high bias, against one too sensitive to the training data, with high variance, to generalize well.

ww.A balance between the price and the qual: A balance between price and quality of purchased data is a procurement matter, while the bias-variance tradeoff concerns model error from being too simple or too flexible.
ww.A balance between training time and test: A balance between training and testing time is about computing cost, and the bias-variance tradeoff is instead about prediction error caused by model complexity.
ww.A balance between the speed of a model a: A balance between speed and memory is a matter of efficiency, whereas the bias-variance tradeoff describes how model simplicity and sensitivity to the data affect errors.

rw: High variance usually means the model fits the training data very closely, even its noise, but performs poorly on new data, which is overfitting.

ww.Is too simple to learn patterns, so it m: A model that is too simple to learn patterns has high bias and underfits, while high variance is the opposite problem of being too sensitive to the data.
ww.Has no errors at all on the training dat: Having no errors on both training and new data would be an ideal model, but high variance means errors on new data are clearly large.
ww.Performs poorly on both training and new: Performing poorly on both training and new data because the model is too simple is underfitting caused by high bias, not by high variance.

rw: High bias means the model is too simple to capture the real patterns, so it underfits and performs poorly on both the training data and new data.

ww.Fits the training data perfectly and fai: Fitting the training data perfectly yet failing on unseen data is overfitting, which comes from high variance and not from high bias.
ww.Has no errors at all on the training dat: Having no errors on training or new data is the ideal case, whereas a high bias model makes clear errors on both because it is too simple.
ww.Learns noise in the training data and fi: Learning the noise in the training data and fitting it too closely is overfitting from high variance, which is the opposite of the underfitting caused by high bias.

rw: Regularization discourages overly complex models, usually by adding a penalty on large weights, which reduces overfitting so the model performs better on new data.

ww.A technique that speeds up training by u: Using larger batches and more hardware speeds up training, but regularization is a different idea aimed at limiting model complexity so it generalizes better.
ww.A technique that increases the model siz: Increasing the model size with more layers and nodes makes a model more complex, which raises the risk of overfitting, while regularization works to limit complexity.
ww.A technique that adds noise to the data: Adding noise to the data to speed learning is not what regularization means, which is a penalty on complexity and not a way to make learning faster.

rw: L1 regularization, called lasso, pushes some coefficients to exactly zero, which removes those features and so performs feature selection as a side effect of fitting.

ww.Making all coefficients larger, so the m: Making all coefficients larger is the reverse of what L1 does, because the L1 penalty pushes coefficients down, and it does not add weight to every feature.
ww.Doubling the learning rate on each pass: Doubling the learning rate is an optimizer setting that controls step size, and it has no connection to the penalty on coefficients that L1 adds.
ww.Removing all training data from the mode: Removing all training data from the model is not part of any regularization method, since L1 adds a penalty on coefficients and leaves the data in place.

rw: L2 regularization, called ridge, shrinks coefficients toward zero without usually making them exactly zero, so all features stay in the model but with smaller weights.

ww.Making the model deeper by adding many m: Making the model deeper with many more layers raises its complexity, which is the reverse of regularization, and L2 is a penalty on large coefficients, not on structure.
ww.Setting all coefficients to one so every: Setting all coefficients to one would give every feature the same weight and ignore the data, whereas L2 only shrinks coefficients toward zero by a small amount.
ww.Deleting features at random from the tab: Deleting features at random describes dropping inputs rather than ridge, whereas L2 keeps every feature and just makes its coefficient smaller through a penalty.
